_meta.purpose: Reviewed record of every public-authority report of a laboratory-confirmed case of the 2026 Bundibugyo virus outbreak outside the DRC. It is the pricing substrate for the international calibration blocks, read only up to each block's source cutoff and frozen by hash, and after each window it is the resolution evidence that lovs/forecast/opsresolver.py reads.
doctrine: One report per authority report that changes a country's cumulative confirmed count. reported_on is the date the report was first published (or first captured by this programme, when the publication date is not stated); confirmed_on is recorded only when the authority states it.
Cited or absent. Every report names at least one source with publisher, URL and publication date; an uncited report fails validation.
Counts never fall and new_confirmed is the change in the running total, so a report cannot be counted twice.
Planned medical evacuations of already-confirmed patients are not reports: they create no country event. They are listed under medical_evacuations for context.
Append only. A correction is a new report or a dated note, never an edit of a published entry.
Silence is not evidence. A pin resolves NO only when a coverage review covers its window; coverage_reviews records which sources were checked through which date.

baseline_affected_countries.basis: Every country that had reported or treated a laboratory-confirmed case of this outbreak before registration, whatever its route: the DRC; Uganda (first case 2026-05-15); France (2026-06-24); Kenya (2026-10-06); Germany and the Netherlands, which treated medically evacuated patients (two US citizens in May and July; a healthcare worker evacuated after testing positive on 2026-09-29); and the United States, which the ECDC outbreak page lists for its evacuated citizens. WHO counts the evacuated patients under the DRC and calls Kenya the fourth country to confirm a case. All seven are in the baseline so that no list artefact or evacuation can resolve a question.
